newsitem.title: Australia: Cricket-Warne strikes as Victoria gain upper hand v NSW.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Warne strikes as Victoria gain upper hand v NSW.

text.p: New South Wales were 228 for seven at tea on the first day of the Sheffield Shield match against Victoria on Friday after leg-spinner Shane Warne took his first first-class wicket in six months during the afternoon session.

Warne, the Victoria captain, only bowled himself for 12 overs during the first two sessions of play as he continues his rehabilitation since undergoing surgery in May to repair ligament damage in the ring finger of his right hand.
After a promising opening spell Warne claimed New South Wales' seventh wicket when he had Anthony Stuart stumped by Darren Berry for a duck on the last ball before tea.
New South Wales had been 114 for three at lunch before Michael Bevan led a top-order fightback, scoring 79 before being caught at second slip from the bowling of Damien Fleming.
Shane Lee was stumped for 40 from the bowling of part-time spinner Matthew Elliott before New South Wales lost Bevan to be 195 for five.
Phil Emery was run out shortly before Warne struck to remove Stuart.
